limitations: The audit is config-level: reachability is derived from the declared network policy (public/allowlist/no-network) plus an unauthenticated endpoint liveness GET from the audit host. It does not docker-exec into a running container.
The probe never sends the audited credential; only an unauthenticated GET /models is issued.

The gate's guarantee is config-level: the patched config carries no real key and no real gateway URL (enforced by re-verification). The mock binds loopback by default; `gate --container-reachable` binds all interfaces and writes a container-reachable host-gateway base URL (host.docker.internal on Docker Desktop, first non-loopback IPv4 on Linux). Linux containers still need host.docker.internal to resolve; automatic extra_hosts rewriting is planned for v0.3.
Mounted credential files and compose env_file credentials cannot be auto-mocked: gate refuses before starting the mock or the eval and requires the mount to be removed or the key inlined.

Built-in gateway endpoints cover OpenRouter and ModelScope; other providers fall back to generic sk-/Bearer and name-based detection with gateway=unknown and no live probe. Under allowlist, an unattributable gateway is treated as reachable (fail closed).
The CI exit code is binary: any finding exits 1, including findings judged not reachable; per-finding reachable verdicts live in the report.
compose env_file entries are read relative to the compose file; the env union includes them, and a declared but unreadable env_file is a hard error.
